government.title: Doping cases before the Asian Games reach a dozen
government.summary: Wushu player Surya Bhanupratap Singh — a 2018 Asiad bronze medallist — tested positive for the SARM Enobosarm and was pulled from India's squad, taking the count of failed dope tests since the Glasgow build-up to 12. Weightlifters, judokas, wrestlers, a shooter, a rower and a runner are among those already out, just over a fortnight before the Aichi-Nagoya Games open (Sept 19–Oct 4).

government.title: Online gaming rules fully in force
government.summary: The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Rules, 2026 are now operational nationwide, formalising the real-money-gaming ban and forcing esports, fantasy-sports and casual-gaming operators to redraw their compliance playbooks.

government.title: Ahmedabad's 2036 Olympic bid pushes on despite IOC caution
government.summary: The government is accelerating stadium and infrastructure plans for a prospective 2036 Games in Ahmedabad even as the IOC has flagged unresolved concerns about the bid's readiness — a governance tug-of-war playing out well ahead of any formal decision.

markets.title: IPL's business value climbs to $20.6bn
markets.summary: Brand Finance now puts the league's business value at $20.6 billion for 2026, with global capital continuing to chase franchise stakes — the clearest sign yet of how far cricket's commercial gravity has pulled ahead of every other Indian sport.

markets.title: Gaming ban breaks a ₹358-crore BCCI–Dream11 deal
markets.summary: The real-money-gaming clampdown has already claimed the BCCI's title sponsorship with Dream11 and knocked listed gaming stocks — Nazara and Delta Corp among them — showing how directly regulation is now reshaping cricket's own sponsorship map.

markets.title: Pro Kabaddi League mid-season
markets.summary: Season 12 continues to draw week-on-week viewership as the league's promoters keep building it out as India's most established non-cricket property.

society.title: “Conspiracy,” “setback”: anger over Commonwealth Games cuts
society.summary: With wrestling, hockey, badminton, table tennis, squash and cricket all trimmed from the shrunken Glasgow 2026 programme, Indian athletes and officials are still fuming — Sharath Kamal calls it the loss of a career “launch pad,” former hockey international Pritam Rani Siwach calls it a “conspiracy,” and federations estimate close to 40 medal chances are gone.

society.title: Women's T20 Asia Cup keeps the crowds coming
society.summary: India Women are through their group fixtures in Dubai, the latest leg of a cricket calendar that keeps pulling fresh domestic attention toward the women's game.

government.title: IOC pushes for talks as US–WADA rift simmers
government.summary: The IOC has called for dialogue between the United States and WADA over their ongoing doping-governance dispute, even as WADA's 2026 Prohibited List sits formally in force worldwide — a reminder that anti-doping's biggest fight right now is political, not chemical.

government.title: World Cup host cities start tallying the returns
government.summary: Early economic-impact accounting from this summer's FIFA World Cup is landing — the New York area alone reports roughly $3.5 billion in impact — as host governments across North America work out what hosting actually bought them.

markets.title: Chelsea's new shirt sponsor is a stablecoin
markets.summary: Circle has struck a one-year front-of-shirt deal putting its USDC stablecoin on Chelsea's men's, women's and academy kits — the club's first marquee sponsor since Three left in 2023, and another sign that finance and fintech brands are the ones filling the space the Premier League's gambling-ad exit opened up.

markets.title: NFL's 2026 season revs up its business machine
markets.summary: The league kicks off its regular season on Sept 9 in Seattle behind a new “The Season Is Your Stage” campaign, opening another year as the world's highest-revenue sports league.

society.title: A Slam field wide open again
society.summary: With Jannik Sinner out injured, Carlos Alcaraz only just back from his own layoff and Aryna Sabalenka labouring through her matches, commentators say the US Open “feels truly open again” — a rare unsettled Slam that's reviving neutral fan interest in the draw.

society.title: Global Chess League returns to Bengaluru
society.summary: Magnus Carlsen headlines Season 4 of the franchise chess league in Bengaluru, the latest example of India positioning itself as a live-event hub for a sport that's rapidly building its own spectator culture.

society.title: Gender-inclusion debate keeps running alongside the games
society.summary: Commentary this week continues to split over how athlete activism on gender and fairness intersects with women's sport itself — an unresolved fight that shows no sign of settling before the next major event does.

opportunities.title: The supplement supply chain behind India's doping wave
opportunities.summary: Most of the 12 pre-Asiad positives look less like deliberate cheating and more like contaminated or mislabelled supplements. Nobody has traced where those products are actually coming from.

opportunities.title: What replaces the Commonwealth Games for India's Olympic sports?
opportunities.summary: Wrestling, hockey and badminton just lost a major platform. Does this quietly accelerate India's push to build kabaddi-style private leagues as substitute exposure — and who's actually funding that shift?

opportunities.title: Is the stablecoin shirt sponsor the next gambling ad?
opportunities.summary: Circle's Chelsea deal is being covered as a novelty. The sharper question — whether crypto sponsorships face the same regulatory arc that pushed betting brands off Premier League shirts — hasn't been asked.

opportunities.title: Cricket's oxygen problem
opportunities.summary: The IPL crossed $20bn in value the same fortnight NADA logged its 12th doping case. A charted look at how completely private capital in Indian sport has concentrated in one sport, leaving Olympic-sport funding and anti-doping infrastructure to the state.

opportunities.title: Who actually pays for the podium?
opportunities.summary: A fresh, benchmarked walkthrough of India's TOPS/SAI funding architecture against China's and Japan's per-athlete spend, timed to land before the Asian Games open on Sept 19.

opportunities.title: Fantasy sport's identity crisis
opportunities.summary: India's 2026 gaming rules were written for real-money betting apps, but esports federations say skill-based and fantasy formats are getting caught in the same net. The regulatory line nobody has drawn clearly yet.
